source_org: Wu et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 127, 180501 (2021)

Rough calibration over all 66 qubits gives two-qubit gate average fidelity 99.24% (p. 2), a different measure (fidelity, not Pauli error) on a different set, so it is not used here. The abstract pairs "66 qubits" with "two-qubit gate (average 99.41%)", which matches the 56-qubit 0.59% figure, so the 56 + 0.59% pair is the one the paper states unambiguously.

source_title: Logical quantum processor based on reconfigurable atom arrays
locator: Abstract (280 physical, 48 logical); Methods p. 12 ("two-qubit gate fidelities in the range F = 99.3% − 99.5%")
notes: Two-qubit error removed from this row: the paper gives "two-qubit gate fidelities in the range F = 99.3% − 99.5%" (Methods p. 12) "under various conditions", with gates on "as many as 160 qubits simultaneously", and cites 99.5% from Evered et al.; none of these is stated for the 280-qubit configuration. The gate figure for this platform is the harvard-evered-2023 row. The 48 logical qubits use error detection with post-selection (runs with detected errors are thrown away), not repeated error correction, so no logical error rate comparable to Google's is reported and none is recorded here.
